title: Power table procedure specification
statement: Let a program $P$ contain the power-table procedure at position $p$, and let the machine limits have memory size $S$, word bound $W$, and depth bound. For an initial memory $\mu$ and natural numbers $\mathrm{dst},L,b$, suppose $S\le W$, the segment of length $L$ starting at $\mathrm{dst}$ fits in memory, and $b^j\le W$ for every $j\le L$. Then calling the procedure at depth $d$ with inputs $(\mathrm{dst},L,b)$ can finish within time $17L+8$, producing the powers $1,b,\ldots,b^{L-1}$ in that segment and preserving all memory locations outside it.
hypotheses_covered: The program has the power-table procedure at index $p$
The machine limits $\mathrm{lim}$ and depth $d$ are fixed
